articles.title: Kannadigas Face Bias in IT? DK Shivakumar Warns Bengaluru Firms After Viral Video | BRASS TACKS
articles.description: Are Kannadigas facing discrimination while applying for jobs in Bengaluru’s IT sector? A viral video by a young woman alleging bias against Kannada-speaking candidates has prompted Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to warn private companies that the government will take appropriate action if deliberate exclusion of local candidates is established. In the video circulating on social media, the woman claimed that some companies were rejecting applicants who listed Kannada as their mother tongue and allegedly favouring candidates from neighbouring states, including Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. She also alleged that recruitment drives were being conducted outside Karnataka and that some candidates were being hired at lower salaries. articles.title: Yogi government emphasizes continuous modernization of the power system; work under Business Plan 2026-27 expedited
articles.description: Lucknow: Under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Uttar Pradesh is making continuous efforts to make the power supply system more robust, modern, and reliable. Under the Business Plan for 2026-27, work to strengthen power substations, lay cables, and improve electricity infrastructure across the state is progressing. These works aim to enhance the capacity of the power distribution system while ensuring safe, smooth, and uninterrupted power supply to consumers. In this regard, teams of Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL) are carrying out night-time maintenance work across the state. They are giving special attention to regularly maintaining power lines, equipment, and the distribution network to keep the power system in better condition. Night maintenance work aims to strengthen the power infrastructure and improve supply reliability. Departmental teams are active across Purvanchal, Paschimanchal, Madhyanchal, Dakshinanchal, and KESCO. The department is improving the distribution system by inspecting and repairing power lines and equipment, along with other essential maintenance work. The department is focused on ensuring the power system continues to operate smoothly while providing a safe, reliable electricity supply to consumers. Power officials are also inspecting substations statewide. During these inspections, officials are reviewing the status of power supply and issuing necessary instructions to the concerned staff. Officials have been directed to pay special attention to maintaining electrical equipment and ensuring the system functions smoothly. Various works are also underway in Uttar Pradesh under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) to modernize the power system. The scheme focuses on strengthening power distribution infrastructure and improving services for consumers. Power department teams are also calling consumers and urging them to pay their electricity bills on time. According to the department, regular bill payments help support the power system's operation and maintenance. The government and the department aim to provide better electricity services to consumers while modernizing the power infrastructure.UPPCL Managing Director Nitish Kumar said the department is continuously working to make the state’s power supply system robust, modern, and reliable. The department is giving special attention to strengthening power substations, laying cables, and improving the electricity distribution network under the Business Plan for 2026-27 and the RDSS scheme. Departmental teams across the state work day and night to maintain power lines and equipment. The department strives to ensure a safe, smooth, and reliable power supply for consumers.

articles.title: Banks pass on rate hikes, but go slow when rates fall; RBI study finds

Amid periods of tightening, lending rates surged significantly, in contrast to the minimal decreases observed during easing. This research highlights the intricate dynamics of interest rate adjustments, particularly affecting sectors like MSMEs.
